slides.title: Tier 2 Vocabulary
bullets: impair (verb): to weaken or damage something so it works less well.
General: Lack of sleep can impair your ability to concentrate in lessons.
Scientific: Alcohol impairs the nervous system, so messages between the brain and body travel more slowly.
Application task: Write a grammatically-correct sentence using this word.

slides.title: Turn and Talk
bullets: Alcohol is legal. Why is it still classed as a drug?
Why is it illegal to sell alcohol to under-18s in the UK?
What effects of alcohol have you seen in adverts, TV or films? Are they accurate?

slides.title: What is alcohol?
bullets: The alcohol in drinks is a chemical called ethanol.
It is a depressant: it slows down the nervous system, including the brain.
It is a legal recreational drug for adults, but it can cause addiction.
The liver breaks down alcohol, and this takes time.

slides.title: Short-term effects
bullets: Slower reaction times
Poor judgement and risk-taking
Loss of balance and coordination; slurred speech
Large amounts: vomiting, unconsciousness, alcohol poisoning
Why is it dangerous to drive after drinking alcohol?

slides.title: Long-term effects
bullets: Liver damage, including cirrhosis (scarring of the liver)
Brain damage and memory problems
Heart disease and high blood pressure
Stomach ulcers and a higher risk of some cancers
In pregnancy: can cause fetal alcohol spectrum disorder

slides.title: Units of alcohol
bullets: 1 unit = 10 ml of pure alcohol
Units = % alcohol × volume (ml) ÷ 1000
Example: a pint (568 ml) of 4% beer = 4 × 568 ÷ 1000 = 2.3 units
UK guideline for adults: no more than 14 units a week, spread over 3 or more days

slides.title: MWB: Calculate the units
bullets: 1. A 330 ml can of 5% lager
2. A 175 ml glass of 12% wine
3. A 25 ml measure of 40% spirit

slides.title: MWB: True or false?
bullets: 1. Alcohol is a stimulant.
2. The liver breaks down alcohol.
3. A pint of beer is always one unit.
4. Alcohol slows your reaction time.
slides.notes: Answers: 1 False (depressant), 2 True, 3 False (depends on % and volume), 4 True
